events.text: You have eaten gates. You have eaten a county's worth of swords, and they went down like anything else, and you were hungry after. Nobody has given you anything since a pair of hands, long ago, rolled you up out of spilled rice. You are not sure why that comes back to you, some nights. To go to a house, you would have to be small again. To be small, you would have to not eat. For a whole winter.
events.arc: A Needle at the Back Door

choices.text: Starve yourself down to the size of a dog

effects.log: It is the worst winter you have ever had, and you get through it by gnawing your own teeth. By spring you can pass under a hedge. Nobody runs from a thing that size; they only throw things. You are almost touched.

choices.text: No. You were made to eat, and there is a mountain over there

effects.log: There is. You start at the top. It tastes of nobody at all, and that is very restful, and it does not seem to help.

events.text: Your first back door. There is a good smell of old hinge. A woman with a lamp comes out for the night soil, and she sees what is on her step, and she does what people do. She screams; she throws the first thing to hand, which is a sickle. It rings on the stone and it lies there. You look at her. You look at it. Nobody has ever thrown you dinner before.
events.arc: A Needle at the Back Door

choices.text: Eat it. It would be rude not to

effects.log: It tastes of her father, and of barley, and of a very long summer. She has stopped screaming, in order to watch. By morning there is a story, and a bad one, and the whole lane has taken in its tools.

choices.text: Set it back on the step, handle first, and go

effects.log: You take a long time about it, with your trunk. She has gone inside by then and is holding the door shut with her whole body. In the morning she will find it. That is more trouble than you have ever gone to about anything.

events.text: You have come to a smithy in the middle of the night. You dream of places like this. The fire is banked, there is a heap of scrap as tall as you are, and you are up to your eyes in it when someone coughs. The old smith is sitting on his anvil in the dark. He has been there for some time. "The slag," he says. "Nobody wants it. Touch my tongs and I will have the monks on you."
events.arc: A Needle at the Back Door

choices.text: Take the slag. Only the slag

effects.log: It is terrible. It tastes of nothing that has ever been loved. He watches you eat it, and nods, and goes to bed. There is a bent nail on the anvil the next time you come by. Neither of you ever mentions it.

choices.text: Take the tongs. Then see what he does about it

effects.log: They are very good tongs: forty years of one right hand. He does nothing at all. He sits there with his empty hand open and looks at you, and you wish he would throw something.

events.text: A beggar is asleep under the bridge, and you can smell what is in the collar of that coat from the far bank. It is one needle, and it is very old. It has been sharpened on a stone so many times that it is hardly more than a thought. This person has mended the same coat for thirty years. There is no other iron here for a day's walk, and it has been a bad month. You are standing over them with your mouth open.
events.arc: A Needle at the Back Door

choices.text: Take it. It is only a needle

effects.log: It is the best thing you have tasted in your whole life. It is thirty years of cold hands. You go on being hungry. They go on with the coat, somehow, with a fishbone, and you see them around, and you take the long way.

choices.text: Shut your mouth, and go and gnaw the bridge pin

effects.log: It is the bridge's; it will not miss it for years. You spend that night with your teeth aching. Someone is snoring below you, in a coat with no holes in it. Going without, for someone else: you turn the idea over all night, like a bad tooth.

events.text: Every hinge in the lane is gone by the autumn, and {npc} has worked out which night you come. {He} is standing at the back door with a lamp, and the lamp is shaking. You can hear {his} teeth. {He} does not scream. {He} bends down, very slowly, and lays one needle on the flat stone, and backs up two steps. "I have only got the two," {he} says. "Please leave the door. It is the door I cannot do without."
events.arc: A Needle at the Back Door

choices.text: Eat it, slowly, there on the stone

effects.log: You make it last. It has sewn a good many things, and lately something in rough hemp. You leave the door. {He} is still standing there, with the lamp, when you look back from the end of the lane.

choices.text: Turn round, and go, and do not come back to that lane

effects.log: You can think of nothing else to do. A person has offered you food, and your whole mouth is shaking. In the morning the needle is still on its stone. {He} takes it in. {He} has only got the two.

events.text: A needle on the stone again, and a bent nail too. {npc} sits up now behind the slit in the door; you can tell by the breathing. You have started to read {him}. Iron keeps everything, in your mouth. The nail is from the roof of a house that was sold. The needle sewed mourning clothes, twice, once for someone young. {He} has told nobody this. You know more about {him} than anyone alive, and you are eating it.
events.arc: A Needle at the Back Door

choices.text: Eat it all, and stay a bit, where {he} can see you

effects.log: You sit down on the step like a dog, with your hedge of needles laid flat, as well as you can. It is some time before the breathing slows. {He} tells you, through the slit, that you have rust on your chin.

choices.text: Leave the needle, and take only the nail. {He} will want that one

effects.log: {He} finds it in the morning. {He} comes out and holds it for a long time, and looks up and down the lane. That night, there are two nails, and no needle, and a very small nod at nobody.

events.text: There is rice in the bowl tonight. {npc} is on the step in plain sight, for the first time, with a spoon. "You cannot eat only that," {he} says. "Nobody could." You have never eaten rice. But {he} is looking past you. Whatever you have become from the neck down, the tail is what it always was: white and sticky. Nobody has looked at it in all these years. {He} holds out the spoon.
events.arc: A Needle at the Back Door

choices.text: Hold still, and turn your tail to {him}

effects.log: {He} presses the warm rice on with the back of the spoon, carefully, like someone mending a wall. You have never felt anything there. You start to shake, all the size of you, and {he} does not move.

choices.text: Pull it away. Nobody touches that

effects.log: You have it under you before you have thought. All your needles have come up, and the spoon is on the ground, and {he} has gone white. {He} goes in. There is a nail on the stone the next night, the same as ever, and that is the worst of it.

events.text: You will never be married, and nobody has suggested it. {npc} has brought out a bowl. It is an old brass one with a chipped rim, and it is, by your reckoning, worth about a month of eating, and {he} has set it down empty on the stone. {He} has been thinking, {he} says. You cannot go on being called "that". {He} puts a nail in the bowl. "Soedol," {he} says. It is what you call a servant's boy. "Soedol. Come and eat."
events.arc: A Needle at the Back Door

choices.text: Come when you are called

effects.log: You have been called a calamity, a mother of calamities, and the end of the kingdom. You come up the step and put your face in the bowl. You do not eat the bowl. It is there the next night, and the next, and it never occurs to {him} to doubt it.

choices.text: Eat the bowl too. You have no name

effects.log: It is good brass, and it tastes of a lot of thin dinners. {He} looks at the stone for quite a long time. {He} goes in, and there is nothing out there after that, on any night, and you were right about what you are.

events.text: The levy men have come with a long chain, to take one from each house for the walls. All six are sleeping off their dinner in the headman's barn, with the chain, the collars and their swords in a heap. {npc}'s nephew is on that chain. There is a bowl on the stone that you have not touched. {npc} has not said anything, and {he} has not looked at you. You have never seen such a beautiful heap.
events.arc: A Needle at the Back Door

choices.text: Eat the chain. Only the chain

effects.log: It takes till dawn, link by link, and you do not wake a soul. They look at their empty hands and at each other. The nephew walks home, the long way. Nobody thanks you, and there are two nails in the bowl.

choices.text: Eat everything. The swords as well

effects.log: It is very fine. They go home with nothing, and the county sends twenty men, and then fifty, and they are asking house by house who it is that has kept all its hinges. It is some time before {npc} can put out a bowl again.

events.text: You have grown. It is what you do. The bowl is hardly a taste now, and you have never said so. But you hear the peddler at the gate, and {npc} asking the price of old nails by the handful. {He} is paying in eggs. {He} does not have that many eggs. You did not know that nails had a price. {He} comes out at dusk with the bowl, as always, and {he} is thinner.
events.arc: A Needle at the Back Door

choices.text: Go up to the old mine at night, and eat there, and come home hungry

effects.log: It is dead rock and it tastes of nothing. You come back to the step every night with a full belly, looking starved, and you eat one nail as if it were a feast. {He} keeps the eggs. {He} never knows, or else {he} never says.

choices.text: Eat what {he} gives you. That is what being fed means

effects.log: You do not know how to refuse it. You eat each nail as slowly as you can. {He} watches you do it with such a look of satisfaction that you could not say, even now, whether you did right.

events.text: Old Bok-sun from across the lane has come round to see {npc}, with a basket, for no reason. Bok-sun sits a long time. The pot is lost, and the door pins, and a late husband's knife. The hinges on this door are looked at, and the worn place on the step, and the chipped bowl. "You have been lucky," says Bok-sun, "in these bad years." The tea is drunk. It is a very small village. {npc} has stopped sewing.
events.arc: A Needle at the Back Door

choices.text: Bring it up. Leave the pot on Bok-sun's step, and the knife

effects.log: It is an ugly business, and there is a lot you would rather not remember. They do not come up quite the same. Bok-sun finds them, dented, shining with spit, on the morning after, and sends over a basket, and in it, under the eggs, is a door pin.

choices.text: Stay out of the lane altogether, and keep your mouth shut

effects.log: You go round by the fields from then on, and you eat nothing that anyone can count. People go on talking. They talk for years. {He} sews with the door shut. It is what it costs, to be anyone's.

events.text: No bowl for eleven days. It is the dead of a very bad winter, {npc} is sick, and you can hear {him} coughing through the wall. You have had nothing for a month. You have got in somehow, and you are in the kitchen, in the dark. The pot is right there. It has cooked every meal of that house for thirty years. You must never eat the house's own iron. You have your mouth on the rim.
events.arc: A Needle at the Back Door

choices.text: Eat it

effects.log: It tastes of every dinner they ever had. It is over very quickly. You are still in the kitchen at dawn when {he} gets up, holding onto the wall, and {he} looks at the place where it was. {He} looks at you. {He} goes out to the step, slowly, and sets down the bowl.

choices.text: Go in to where {he} is lying, and put your head down by the mat

effects.log: You are far too big for that room. You let {him} see the whole of it, the size, the teeth, and how much you want that pot. {He} opens {his} eyes. "I know," {he} says. "I have always known. There are three nails under the mat. Go on."

choices.text: Get out. Go now, and do not stop till you are a province away

effects.log: You break the door doing it, the one {he} asked you to leave. You run all that night. You have never been so sure of anything you did for anyone. {He} gets well, you hear. {He} goes on setting out the bowl for a long time, and then you do not hear.

events.text: You wake on the step with a sweet taste in your mouth: ash wood, old sweat, a whole lifetime of springs. You are chewing. It is the plough. The share is half gone, the ploughing is tomorrow, and {npc} has come out into the grey with the bowl in {his} hands. You did not decide this. You were asleep. You have never been so full. {He} looks at the plough, and at you, and {he} does not drop the bowl.
events.arc: A Needle at the Back Door

choices.text: Spit it back. Take it to the smith yourself

effects.log: It is hard to bring up, and it comes out wrong, a warm lump. You carry it to the old smith's door and you wait in the road until the smith has stopped swearing. It makes half a plough, and a bad one. {He} ploughs with it for nine years.

choices.text: Stay. Walk the furrow yourself, with your own teeth

effects.log: You pull it, all that day, your jaw in the ground, up and down, and the whole village comes out to look. It is the worst-ploughed field in the county and it comes up thick. {He} walks behind you with the seed. There is no hiding any of it now.

choices.text: Go. Before you wake up with the door in your mouth

effects.log: You leave the half that is left, and you go. There is one thing you will always be, and you know that, now, for a fact. The bowl sits on the stone with a nail in it until somebody's dog takes it away.

events.text: Someone is screaming in the house in the small hours, and it is {npc}. {bk_child}, not yet walking, got hold of the rice bowl, and there was a needle in it, dropped from the mending, and now it is gone. They are holding the small thing upside down. You put your face to the crack of the door. You can smell that needle. It is going along quite calmly in there, like someone on a good road.
events.arc: A Needle at the Back Door

choices.text: Sit at the door all night, and do not eat

effects.log: It stops at about dawn, in the jaw, and it stays there. {bk_child} wakes up, hungry, and in a very good temper. {He} checks everything, twice, and {he} comes out to you, shaking, and for some reason {he} sets down the bowl and sits next to it.

choices.text: Push your trunk in under the door, to try to draw it out

effects.log: You could draw every needle in that house. It comes along a little way, and the small thing howls. {npc} comes at you with a broom, the first time that {he} has ever dared. You stop. The needle goes back where it was going. You will never know if you should have.

events.text: {bk_child} has found the back step. A small person sits down next to you on the stone and looks in your bowl with interest. There is one nail in it. You have been hungry since before anyone can remember. Two small fingers go into the bowl, come out with the nail, and hold it up to you. It is wet. {npc} is in the kitchen, and you can hear that {he} has not noticed yet.
events.arc: A Needle at the Back Door

choices.text: Take it from those fingers. Very, very gently

effects.log: You have taken swords from generals with less care. It tastes of milk and dirt. {bk_child} is delighted, and goes in, and comes back with a spoon. {npc} is never going to hear about this, if you have your way.

choices.text: Take the bowl in your teeth, and move it out of reach

effects.log: There is an outcry, which brings out {npc}, who looks at the bowl up on the wall, and looks at you. {He} nods. It is the first time you have ever been thanked for not eating something. It does not stop you wanting to.

events.text: {bk_child} is seven, and has lost a tooth, a small white one, like anybody. You have been watching for seven years for a little grey. Last week {bk_child} sat on a darning needle and yelled the house down. There was a needle in the rice once, you recall. {bk_love} has explained to you, with some embarrassment, where most things go in the end, in the ordinary course of events.
events.arc: A Needle at the Back Door

choices.text: Eat your nail. Be pleased

effects.log: You are. Nobody is ever going to set out a bowl for that child, or hunt it, and it can go near a smithy whenever it wants to. It has come out and thrown a stone at you, and missed. You take that very kindly.

choices.text: Sniff the small white tooth, just to be sure, where it was thrown on the roof

effects.log: You go up there at night, and you have it in your mouth for a while. It tastes of nothing that you can use. You put it back carefully, where the magpies will find it. It is a good thing that nobody saw you at that.

events.text: The third hungry winter, and nothing on the stone for nine nights. {bk_love} has nothing left in the house but the door. You have stayed anyway, flat on the step, too hollow to go up the mountain. The door opens by a hand. {bk_child}, who is seven, comes out in the snow, squats, and takes something out of one cheek. It is a nail, bitten clean through by small grey teeth. You are being given the larger half.
events.arc: A Needle at the Back Door

choices.text: Eat it, and let {bk_child} see you eat it

effects.log: It tastes of hunger and of great care. {bk_child} watches, nods, and sits down against you to eat the other half, with a small crunch. {bk_love} is at the door, and has seen, and says only: "How long?" There will be mouths like that after you are gone, and some of them will share.

choices.text: Push it back. That is the one thing you will not take

effects.log: It lands in the snow. {bk_child} picks it up, gives you a look of pure contempt, and puts it down again, closer. You push it back. It goes on until dark. In the end the child eats it and goes in, with a look back. The blood will go on, and it does not need your leave.

events.text: Somewhere in these last years {npc} stopped being able to see the eye of a needle. {He} comes out at dusk with a bad hip and a spoon of rice, pats it onto your tail, and goes in. A little later {he} comes out and does it again. "Have you eaten?" {he} asks. {He} has asked that of everyone {he} has ever known. It is the only question there is. "Soedol," {he} says. "Did you eat?"
events.arc: A Needle at the Back Door

choices.text: Bow your head, and take it. As many times as {he} comes

effects.log: Your tail has got as big as a sheaf. You do not eat iron anywhere {he} could know of. The neighbours have started to bring you rice, on {his} behalf, so that {he} will have some to give you. It is the most anyone has ever fed you, and it is all going to waste.

choices.text: Fetch {his} needle, the last one, and thread it with your trunk

effects.log: It takes the whole of one night, with the trunk that could drink a river. {He} sews badly, by feel. {He} sews something for you, it seems, which goes nowhere near you. You wear it. You do not know what it is, and you have not eaten it.

events.text: They have shut the door of that house for the mourning. It is the first time in all these years that there has been no one on the step at dusk. You come anyway. You come for forty-nine days, and you sit there. {bk_love} had a needle-case, and someone has left it out for you on the stone. It is hard to say who. There is one needle in it. It is very small, and it will be the last thing you ever taste of {bk_love}.
events.arc: A Needle at the Back Door

choices.text: Eat it, as slowly as anything can be eaten

effects.log: It takes nine years. You keep it in your cheek, where you can find it. It tastes of mourning hemp, and every shirt in the valley, and a spoon. When it is gone, you sit there a while, and you discover that you are hungry. You are so angry about that.

choices.text: Do not eat it. Lay it back on the stone, and eat nothing

effects.log: You stop. You lie down at the back of the house, and you do not eat for as long as you can, which is nothing at all to a thing that cannot be killed. It does at least hurt. The children start to leave you nails, and you do not touch them, for now.

events.text: Sixty years on, and they are still at it. There is a family in that house, of {bk_child}'s blood, with big jaws and heavy feet, who break a good many stools. Each night somebody sets a bowl on the back step with a nail in it. It is for rats, they say, if you ask. Nobody has ever asked what kind of rat. They are not curious people. You have seldom felt so well looked after.
events.arc: A Needle at the Back Door

choices.text: Come for it, as small as you can, and let them talk

effects.log: You do, some nights. A child at an upstairs window gets a look at you, and it does not scream, and it goes to bed thinking. There is a second nail in the bowl after that. Their luck with hinges is remarkable.

choices.text: Leave it for a while, and go and eat a mountain

effects.log: It stays there rusting, for four years, and they go on putting out a new one each night. You hear about the pile. Someone makes a joke about rats. It is hard to say which of you is keeping the other going.

events.text: You hear it on the wind off a battlefield, which is where you get most of your news. There is an officer in the south, of {bk_child}'s blood, and no smith in that province will let them in. Their sword has an odd scalloped look to its edge. They get through about one a year. They sink in a river like an anvil, and they are careful around campfires. You feel like somebody's grandparent.
events.arc: A Needle at the Back Door

choices.text: Eat the enemy's armoury, one dark night, as a present

effects.log: It is a very fine one. In the morning the whole of the other army is holding its hands out and looking at them. The officer looks at the tracks. They set out a bent horseshoe at the edge of camp, and go back to bed.

choices.text: Stay out of it. They can look after their own dinner

effects.log: They can. You hear that the scalloping has got a good deal neater. Somebody must have shown them. You go on past that province, by the long way, chewing, and you are extremely pleased.

events.text: You gave up back doors long ago. It is late, you are very large, and you are in a scrapyard at a river town when somebody comes over the fence with a sack. {npc} steals iron. {He} stops dead. {His} knees are going. {He} looks at the size of you, and at the fence, a long way off. Then, very carefully, {he} takes a horseshoe out of the sack and slides it over with {his} foot. "Go halves," {he} says.
events.arc: A Needle at the Back Door

choices.text: Eat it. Tell {him} what it is {he} is feeding

effects.log: It takes all night and a lot of pointing. {He} sits on the sack and asks about prices. You have never met anyone so unimpressed. There is a bowl at that fence, thereafter, of a kind: it is a dented helmet, and it was certainly someone else's.

choices.text: Push it back with your trunk, and go

effects.log: You go out through the fence, and you take some of it with you. {He} sells the horseshoe. You hear that {he} goes about saying that you owe {him} one.

events.text: Someone walks up into the old mine where you are chewing, with a lamp and no sword, and sits on a rock. They are too heavy for how they look; the rock says so. They open a small cloth, take out a needle gone quite black, and lay it on the ground. They have one grey tooth, at the front. "It has been in the family," they say. "I kept it in my mouth so it would not rust. Have you eaten?"
events.arc: A Needle at the Back Door

choices.text: Eat it, with all the manners you have got

effects.log: You have not had a better needle since the first. You could not say what it has been through. They watch you, with interest, and at last they take a nail out of their sleeve and crunch it, companionably. Neither of you has anything to add.

choices.text: Push it back, and bring them the best of the seam

effects.log: It takes you till evening to find it, a lump as big as a head, and it tastes of the first days of the world. They are not at all surprised. They have brought a spoon, and they stay for the whole of the week, and they eat you out of a whole gallery.

events.text: Your first tooth came at three months, and it was grey, and it is still there, at the front. Today you are eating your soup in the usual way, and {npc} has stopped talking to look at the spoon. There is a bite out of it. You had not noticed. You can feel the bit in your cheek. It tastes a little like your aunt. {npc} holds out {his} hand, palm up, under your chin. "Spit," {he} says.
events.arc: Blood of the Swallowed Needle

choices.text: Spit. Ask {him} why it tastes like that

effects.log: "Everything does," says {npc}, looking at the piece of spoon. That is all you get, and {he} goes back to {his} soup. {He} gets you a wooden one, and you get the feeling that a number of wooden spoons have come down in this family.

choices.text: Swallow, and open your mouth to show there is nothing there

effects.log: You show {him} your whole mouth. {He} looks in with care, and then {he} looks at the spoon, and sighs. You feel very clever. You have a stomach ache for the first time in your life, and it is not from that.

events.text: New Year, and the village has put up the jumping board. You wait your turn and get up on one end, with a little girl from the Yun house on the other. You jump. The girl goes up very high, and comes down in the Baks' pear tree, unhurt and very surprised. They try it again. The plank goes this time, right in the middle, and it was a good plank. {npc} is looking at your feet.
events.arc: Blood of the Swallowed Needle

choices.text: Say that you are sorry, and stay to mend it

effects.log: You mend it, and it is quite strong, and you are never again allowed on that end. The Yun girl tells everyone it was never a better day. People have started to ask you what you weigh.

choices.text: Say that the plank was rotten. Walk lightly from then on

effects.log: You make a study of walking lightly. You go up on your toes across every floor. It gives you a very fine walk, of which people take note, and very sore calves, of which nobody does.

events.text: They have sent you to the smith with a broken hoe. You are only standing in the door. It smells so good that your teeth hurt. The old man at the anvil straightens up very slowly, and sees what your eyes are doing. All the tongs on the wall have started to hum, very faintly. The smith takes the hoe from you and shuts the door. {npc} comes to get you. {He} has been expecting this.
events.arc: Blood of the Swallowed Needle

choices.text: Ask {him} why the man looked at you like that

effects.log: "Because that man's grandfather did," says {npc}. "And the grandfather before. They keep a list." You stand there for a while in the road, and it is the first you have heard of any list. You can still smell it from there.

choices.text: Say that you were only there about the hoe

effects.log: You do not go back. Someone else takes the hoes from then on. You walk the long way round by the mill, and the wind is always wrong, and you get used to that, the way you might get used to a bad tooth.

events.text: Your sixteenth harvest, and somebody's sickle comes round too wide. It takes you deep in the arm. Everyone is shouting. It does not bleed as it should. There is a thin grey line along the cut, already closing, and what you mainly feel is hungry. You seem to have bitten the sickle. {npc} takes you by the good arm. "Come and sit," {he} says, "and I will tell you about a needle."
events.arc: Blood of the Swallowed Needle

choices.text: Hear all of it

effects.log: A back door, a bowl, a name for a servant's boy, and a child called {bk_line} who swallowed what it should not have. And the one who came for the bowl: {bk_anc}. Then {npc} holds a coal up in the tongs, near your arm, and you find out about the other half. You did not know that anything could hurt like that. "Fire," says {npc}. "Remember."

choices.text: Say it is a scratch, and go back to the field

effects.log: You go back, and you bind it up, and you take very great care to bleed. They all say how lucky you were. You pick up a new sickle by the handle. You are looking at it for rather too long, and you put it down.

events.text: You need a blade. There are four smiths in this district. The first is out. The second has a sudden illness in the household. The third is young and has not been told, starts on it, and the father comes out of the back room, looks at you, and takes it out of the young hand. The fourth has put a sign on the door. You cannot read it, but {npc} can. It says, more or less: no.
events.arc: Blood of the Swallowed Needle

choices.text: Stand in the road in front of the sign, for a day, and be seen

effects.log: They all have to walk around you to get in. By evening a very old man comes out with a very old knife, and puts it on the ground, and goes back in. You do not know if that was a gift, or something else. You do not eat it, for a week.

choices.text: Buy from a peddler, like anyone, and pay too much

effects.log: It is a bad knife, and you pay well over what it is worth, and it is yours. The peddler looks at your teeth while you count out the silver. The peddler adds a bit to the price, and you say nothing.

choices.text: Go without. You have got on all right so far

effects.log: You make do with a sharpened bit of oak, and people laugh. It has a good edge for about a morning. You keep it in your belt. Your fingernails have got rather long and rather grey.

events.text: A drunk at the village gate has an old army sword, and the whole lane is behind its doors. You only came out for water. The drunk comes at you. You have a bucket in one hand, so you put up the other. It is a real blade and a real swing. It lands on your forearm and stops, with a sharp clear sound. Now it is half a sword, and the rest of it seems to be in your mouth. {npc} has seen. Everybody has.
events.arc: Blood of the Swallowed Needle

choices.text: Hand the drunk the hilt, and say to go home

effects.log: The drunk takes it, and goes home. There is a very long silence on the lane, and then a lot of talk. They are all quite glad about it. They ask you to stand at the gate at the next festival, and nobody sits next to you.

choices.text: Howl, and clutch your arm, and let them bind it

effects.log: You howl very convincingly. A great many people have seen what you would like them to think that they saw. {npc} comes and does the binding up, with a great many rags, tutting, and says it is a miracle you still have the arm.

events.text: A small one in the Yun house has not slept for a month. Somebody's grandmother comes up the lane in the rain to see you, and will not sit. There are old screens in the great houses, says the grandmother, with an animal painted on them, and bad dreams will not go in where it is. The grandmother has no screen. {npc} says nothing. "You would only need to sit there," says the grandmother. Your teeth are not looked at.
events.arc: Blood of the Swallowed Needle

choices.text: Go and sit by the small one, all night, and see

effects.log: You sit there on the floor with your big hands. Around the third hour you feel something come in by the door, and stop, and go out. It tastes, oddly, of iron. The small one sleeps for two days. People start to come up the lane, at dusk.

choices.text: Tell the grandmother it is an old wives' story, and shut the door

effects.log: You lie awake, with the rain coming down. It is the sort of thing that you could only have got from someone who knows. You hear the screams across the lane, at the third hour, for another month. Your teeth ache all that time.

events.text: You have kept it from {npc} for years: the nail after dinner, out in the woodshed, like a drunk. You have thought that you were very careful. Tonight you come in to your rice, and {he} sits down opposite with {his} own, and does not look up. On top of your rice, in the very middle, laid straight, there is one clean nail. {He} goes on eating. "Eat," {he} says.
events.arc: Blood of the Swallowed Needle

choices.text: Eat it, and tell {him} all about the back door

effects.log: It crunches. It is the loudest thing that you have ever heard. Then you tell {him}, about the bowl and the name and the rest, with your mouth full. {He} says that it was the kitchen knife that gave you away. {He} buys them by the sack now, and {he} is quite cross about the price.

choices.text: Move it to the side of the bowl, and ask about the weather

effects.log: You leave it there through the whole of the meal, and it is the hardest thing that you have ever done. {He} clears the bowls, and {he} says nothing. There is another one the next night. It has become the way that you two talk.

events.text: {npc} has come home from lessons with a note about the teacher's inkstone weights. You look in {his} mouth. You need not have. There it is at the front: small, grey and very pleased with itself. You know where this goes. The smiths keep a list. {He} looks up at you with {his} jaw going slowly round on something, and it is not a sweet.
events.arc: Blood of the Swallowed Needle

choices.text: Sit {him} down. Teach {him} what may be eaten, and what never

effects.log: Old nails, yes. Dead iron from the hills. Never the pot, never the plough, never the hinge of a house that has fed you, and keep away from a fire. {He} recites it back to you, with {his} mouth full, like a very small monk.

choices.text: Hold out your hand. "Spit"

effects.log: {He} spits. You give {him} a wooden spoon, of the sort that comes down in your line. {He} looks at it, and at you, and {he} starts going out to the woodshed after dinner. You do not say that you have noticed. You know what is out there.

events.text: {npc} buys bones. {He} has good brass scales at {his} belt and a dry, cheerful way of sizing you up. There is a sword-smith in the capital, {he} tells you, who will pay a hundred times the weight for a thighbone like yours, ground into the steel: it makes a blade that cannot be broken. The trouble is getting it. {He} sets the scales down on the inn bench. "Humour me," {he} says. "Stand on that."
events.arc: Blood of the Swallowed Needle

choices.text: Eat the scales, and then see about {him}

ok.log: The scales go first; they taste of a great many bad bargains. {He} backs out of the inn with {his} hands up, laughing, and without any brass. {He} looks more interested than ever. "A very good sign," {he} calls, from out in the road.

fail.log: {He} does not bother with a blade. {He} has a lit torch from the inn wall in {his} hand before you are off the bench, and {he} knows where to put it. You come round in the ditch, with your shoulder burned, and you know now that {he} has been told about the fire.

choices.text: Stand on it, and hold your breath, and think of feathers

effects.log: You cannot do anything about the feathers. It goes down with a thump. {He} looks at the weight, and at you, and whistles, and writes that down. {He} buys you a bowl of tea, and tells you that you should eat more greens.

events.text: {npc}, grey now, sits on your wall at evening with the brass scales across {his} knees and four men with torches in the lane behind {him}. They are in no hurry. {He} has come to like you, in the way one likes a very fine piece of ore. "One thighbone," {he} says. "You would hardly feel it. Or I can have all of it, tonight, and it would be a pity about the thatch."
events.arc: Blood of the Swallowed Needle

choices.text: Go through them, torches and all

ok.log: They had not thought you would come straight at the fire. You feel every bit of it. You are grey and black and smoking, and you have got the scales in your teeth, and the men have gone. {He} has not. {He} sits on the ground, and {he} looks at the last of the brass with real regret.

fail.log: You get three of the torches. It is the fourth that does it. You wake up by the stream, a long time later, a good deal lighter than you were. {He} has been most careful. There is a little silver on your chest, with a note, for the weight.

choices.text: Send out a jawbone instead, an old one, from the family's grave

effects.log: It is a terrible thing to do, and you do it with your own hands, up on the hill, by night. {He} weighs it, there on the wall, and looks at you for a long time. {He} bows to it, quite properly, and {he} goes. You will have to tell someone, some day, and it is not going to be today.

events.text: You have started waking up in strange places. Tonight it is the magistrate's armoury, at the third watch. You are sitting on the floor in your night clothes beside a rack of good spears, a fair number of the heads are gone, and your mouth is full. For the first time since you were born, you are not hungry. You had no idea. Someone outside has started to shout. {npc} is at the window, beckoning.
events.arc: Blood of the Swallowed Needle

choices.text: Finish that rack, first. Then go

effects.log: They never do find out. It sets the county's accounts back years. {npc} gets you home in a cart under some sacks, and {he} looks at you as you lie there, humming. You do not recall when you last slept so well.

choices.text: Spit it out on the floor, and go. Eat plain rice for a year

effects.log: Your teeth ache for a whole year, right up behind the eyes. You chew on nothing. You are tied to your bed at night by a rope, and in the morning there is not much left of it, and it is, at any rate, not iron.

events.text: An army is going through the valley on the high road, and you can hear it from the kitchen. It sounds like a very great many spoons. Three days of it: forty thousand swords, all the wagons, every kind of horseshoe. You have stopped eating. You have stopped pretending to. You would only have to walk up there tonight. {npc} has come out and sat down in your way, on the step, with a bowl of rice.
events.arc: Blood of the Swallowed Needle

choices.text: Go around {him}, up the hill, in the dark

effects.log: You never tell anybody about it. There is a battle the week after, which goes very strangely, with a great many soldiers holding out their empty hands. It is put down to Heaven. You have a grey shine on your teeth for months, and the smiths all shut their doors as you go past.

choices.text: Sit down next to {him}, and eat the rice

effects.log: You eat it all, a grain at a time, with your hands shaking. It takes about three days. {He} goes on bringing more. Then one morning there is nothing up there except a dusty road, and it is very quiet, and you are so hungry that you could cry.

events.text: {npc} brings you to a mine given up long before your line began. You go in with a lamp, a long way, and you see the walls. They are not cut. They are bitten: great curved marks as high as a roof, tunnel after tunnel, into the dark. Far in, on a flat stone, there is a bowl, rusted almost through. {npc} takes a needle from {his} collar, and holds it out to you. {bk_anc} used to eat here.
events.arc: Blood of the Swallowed Needle

choices.text: Lay it in the bowl, and step back two paces

effects.log: Nothing comes. You wait until the oil is low. When you turn around at the bend, and look back with the last of the lamp, you could not swear that the needle is still there. {npc} tells you not to go back to see. You do go. It is not.

choices.text: Eat it yourself, there, in front of the bowl

effects.log: It tastes of someone's mourning, an impossibly long time ago. You know exactly who. You stand there with your mouth full of it, and you are crying, and {npc} takes the lamp a little way off and looks at the wall.

events.text: Behind the old market town there is a hill with no iron in it or near it, and nobody will say why. {npc} walks you up in the rain. It is not really a hill. There is a long back under the grass, a great heap of old rust, with hilts standing out of it like dead thistles. At the far end something short lies in the wet, white and sticky, and it moves. What remains of {bk_anc} has heard you come.
events.arc: Blood of the Swallowed Needle

choices.text: Press a spoonful of rice onto it, with the back of the spoon

effects.log: You have brought rice, for some reason. Nobody told you to. You do it carefully, like someone mending a wall. Nothing happens for a long time. Then all down that whole long hill, you hear something give a very deep and rusty sigh.

choices.text: Pull one of the hilts out. It may be that you will need it

effects.log: It comes out with a groan, and a very good blade comes after it, older than the kingdom. It fits your hand, and you already know it, and it knows you. The hill does not object. {npc} asks you, on the way down, if you plan to feed that or be fed by it.

events.text: You bit through the well-chain this morning, without noticing. {npc} sits with you on the back step. "It will not stop," {he} says. "There is a monk at the river who knows the old way: a staff across the back, and up it comes, every needle your line ever ate. Or there is the road, and the armies. You know that way." {He} turns a nail over in {his} fingers. "Or there is the bowl. But nobody has kept to that."
events.arc: Blood of the Swallowed Needle

choices.text: Go to the monk. Bring it all up

effects.log: It takes three days and a bucket. There is a good deal more of it than you would have thought. You weigh so little, after that, that you trip going down the step. They give you a bowl of rice. You are hungry in the ordinary way, for the first time, and it goes away when you eat.

choices.text: Take the road. Eat what you like

effects.log: You leave at dusk. There is a whole country of it, and it tastes of everyone. They tell it in the villages with their doors shut: a thing that walks at night and cannot be killed. It leaves the hinges on some houses, for no reason they can see.

choices.text: Eat only what is put out for you. Every night, for good

effects.log: You have to be told, and you have to ask, and you go hungry between. {npc} goes in and comes out with the old chipped bowl, and {he} sets it down, and puts a nail in it, and sits back, looking rather pleased. "Well?" says {npc}.

events.text: It took some getting used to. You float in the river, a little, and panic. You went to the smith for a knife, and the smith looked you up and down and took your money, and you stood in that smithy for an hour, breathing. It smells of hot metal. You cut yourself on the kindling, and it bleeds red for ages. {npc} comes and laughs at you, and brings a rag.
events.arc: Blood of the Swallowed Needle

choices.text: Buy another knife. Buy a very nice one

effects.log: You have become someone who has opinions about knives, and who cuts up an onion very well. Nobody has ever had so much fun with an onion. You keep the old wooden spoon in a box.

choices.text: Go and sit by the back step, at dusk, for no reason

effects.log: There is nothing there, and nothing is coming. So one can miss being hungry. You sit there until it has got dark and {npc} calls you in. It is a very good dinner, and you are only a little sorry.

events.text: You stopped using doors some time ago. They say at the fairs that there is one in the north who goes through arsenals like a bad year. You come back in the dark of the moon, as far as the edge of the yard. There is a light. {npc} has got very slow. You can smell a nail on a stone from a long way off, and {he} says, not at all loudly, to the dark: "Did you eat?"
events.arc: Blood of the Swallowed Needle

choices.text: Come up and take it. Say nothing

effects.log: It is a very small nail. You have had a garrison's worth this month. You eat that one last, and slowly, and you are gone before {he} has got back up the step. You still taste that one.

choices.text: Leave something on the stone, for a change

effects.log: It takes some thought. You leave a helmet with gold on it, and the next time a general's seal, and {he} uses it to hold down the pickle lids. You watch that from the hedge, and you do not know what the feeling is for.

events.text: You have a very strict arrangement, and it is ridiculous. You eat only what you are given. So people give it to you. They come up the lane at dusk with a rusted chain, or a knife that did something, or a thing out of a bad dream. They set it on the stone and go, not looking back. {npc} asks if you have eaten. The magistrate has started sending round the old leg-irons.
events.arc: Blood of the Swallowed Needle

choices.text: Eat what they bring, and do not ask what it was

effects.log: You always know. It is all in the taste. You have swallowed the worst things in three counties, and they sleep better for it, and you do not. It is, on the whole, a very good living.

choices.text: Tell the one with the knife that you will not take it

effects.log: They stand there on the step, with it in their hand. It is the first time anyone has been refused. They go home with it, and they come back in a month, and they tell you what they did. That is when you eat it.

events.text: You have one tooth left, and it is the grey one. You could go on for a long while on that. The little ones want to know how much you weigh, and they have a list of what you have broken, which you are not supposed to know about: nine stools and a bridge. {npc} reads it out, and says that it has a certain style. You ask to hear about the bridge again.
events.arc: Blood of the Swallowed Needle

choices.text: Tell them about the bridge

effects.log: You tell it wrong, and better. It is a very long bridge by now, and it was full of soldiers. The small ones lean on you, as you would lean on a warm wall, and you do not shift a hair in case they stop.

choices.text: Let them weigh you. It is only fair

effects.log: They bring the rice scale, and it takes six of them. The scale does what it does. There is a long, awed silence. You are delighted, and {npc} can be heard laughing through the wall.

events.text: It is getting cold for it, but you are out on the back step at dusk, wrapped up, since they could not keep you in. The stone there is worn in a shallow dip, about the size of a bowl. You had never really looked. It must have taken a long time. {npc} has come out behind you with a blanket and something on a spoon. {He} sits down. {He} is about to ask you the only question there is.
events.arc: Blood of the Swallowed Needle

choices.text: Say that you have eaten

effects.log: It is not true, and {he} knows that. You say it anyway, as you have heard it said. {He} leaves the spoon on the step, in case. You sit there together, and it gets dark. A small grey moth comes and looks at the spoon.

choices.text: Open your mouth

effects.log: You have not done that since you were very small. {He} looks at you. {He} does not laugh. It is plain rice, and it is warm, and you can taste whose hands it was, all the way down to the first ones.
